acts.desc: Ira recounts the story of William Cimillo, a New York bus driver who snapped one day, left his regular route, and drove his municipal bus down to Florida.
acts.label: Prologue
Act One
acts.desc: Radio Diaries ’ Joe Richman continues William Cimillo’s story and talks to his two sons about what it was like to have lived through the drama that ensued after their father’s big journey. (11 1/2 minutes)
acts.credits: By Joe Richman, Sarah Kate Kramer
acts.title: Busman’s Holiday

acts.label: Act Two
acts.desc:
Producers Jonathan Goldstein and Sean Cole were fascinated by a recent Pew Research statistic
stating that 9% of Americans want to travel through time. So they decided to hit the streets and
ask people—is it true? Do you want to travel through time? And what period of time would you travel to?
acts.title: Where We're Going, We Don't Need Roads

acts.label: Act Three
acts.desc: Tina Dupuy was a teenage alcoholic. She joined Alcoholics Anonymous at the age of 12, got sober by 13. And she learned to tell the hell out of her story at speaking events. She even became "AA Famous." But at the age of 33, she had a sudden realization that made her question the very story she was famous for.
acts.title: The Wisdom to Know the Difference
